sections.text: Passion, engendered by thirst for pleasure and attachment, binds the soul through its fondness for activity.
But Ignorance, the product of darkness, stupefies the senses in all embodied beings, binding them by chains of folly, indolence and lethargy.
सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत।
Purity brings happiness, Passion commotion, and Ignorance, which obscures wisdom, leads to a life of failure.

So we had been discussing chapter 14, Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga, the Yoga of Trigunas. We had just completed the Kshetrakshatragna Vibhaga, the differentiation between the field and its knower. We have seen that this world of ours is made up of two things.
One is the field and its knower. In my case, I the knower of my world. And then we have also seen at the macro level, its a Purusha and Prakriti, two entities which makes this manifest world apparent to me. Prakriti is the nature, the manifest world, and Purusha is the unmanifestation which is making this Prakriti animated.
So this understanding of Purusha and Prakriti -- now we can use it to our advantage. As Bhagawan says, we can only understand it if we know the nature of this Prakriti. Prakriti, even in our vernacular language, refers to anybodys inherent qualities and nature -- thats his Prakriti.
Also in Gujarati they say -- Im sure its in other languages too. Pranayani, Prakruti, Sathya Jay, that this breath and my quality, they go together, they remain embedded in me. So knowing this Prakriti can certainly be a big help in my spiritual quest of knowing myself.
So this chapter talks about Gunatraya, the three Gunas of the Prakriti. Prakriti is me as this body, mind and intellect. This world as I see it is all-pervading, just as the nature of Brahman is.
And as we have said, both the Purusha and Prakriti are beginningless because both are the nature of Brahman, which is beginningless. Something which is beginningless in whatever format it is presented remains beginningless. Therefore, Prakriti is beginningless. Purusha is beginningless.
In my quest of understanding myself, myself is beginningless. Where did I create this misunderstanding that Im limited and Im going through these ups and downs in my life? Im Going through these sorrows and happiness, the spurts of little happiness and then long period of pursuit of happiness. Bhagavan said that understanding this nature of this Prakriti will be helpful.
Bhagawan said, I am the Mahat Yoni Brahman. I, the Brahman in the form of a Prakriti is the womb of all the beings. No being or thing can come into existence unless the Purusha and Prakriti come together.
So see, anywhere you see a thing or being coming into existence, consider that as the union of the Purusha and Prakarati, that unmanifest and manifest coming together creates a new creation. Wherever there is a birth taking place, consider that it is coming from my womb, the universal womb. And then you say, I am the Sid giver, Father. Prakriti is the womb and Purusha is the father.
Therefore, in our all vernacular language is Mother Nature, Mother Earth. And Bhagavan is Pita. Bhagavan is my father. Prakriti is my mother, comes directly from this verse from Bhagavad Gita.
So this nature, Mother Nature, when it comes to me, creates this body, mind and intellect. When I was born, what I was born with is this body, which continues to grow and decay. I was born with this mind and intellect, which at the rudimentary level grew into who I think I am today.
If I know the nature of this Prakriti, it will help me understand who I am. So the next three verses tell us the nature of Prakriti. Swattam Rajah, Tama, iti, Gunaha, Prakriti, Sambhavah.
The three Gunas which we see in this world, in almost everything that we can observe, are Sattva, rajas and Tamas. They are born out of Prakriti. This manifest world becomes manifest because of these Gunas.
Take these three gunas away and there is no world -- only the unmanifest remains. So what is the first? Sattva -- purity, awareness, knowledge, luminosity. A thing comes into existence for me when I become aware of it.
We went on a cruise about two years ago and realized at the last minute that we needed some cash. So I went to the ATM, but it was Sunday and my car just wouldnt work. So I finally called my client in Baltimore -- Mike, can you have $300 in cash for me? Ill give you a check when I come there.
So anyway, he had three crisp $100 notes ready for me in an envelope. I went there, collected it, gave him a check and went on the cruise. We never used that money.
It was sealed in that envelope when we came back, and we forgot all about it. Those $300 never existed for us for all this time. Because we had forgotten about it.
Then one day we opened it -- $300 in it. We are suddenly $300 richer. They did not exist for us until then.
Then one day Mina said, I gave you that $200. What did you do with it? Well I said I have it. Ill give it back to you if you want.
That money came into existence when I became aware of it, when Mina became aware of it. Till that time it did not exist. Sattvam -- unless you are aware of this world, the world does not come into existence for you.
So it is for her, for him, and everybody else. When we all become unaware of this world, it ceases to exist for us. So Sattva is the first quality of Prakriti.
In this nature, we are aware of each other and therefore we exist for each other. Next is Rajas and third is Tamas. We have heard it many, many times before.
But he said they are Prakriti Sambhavah. These gunas are born out of Prakriti. My Prakriti is that I become aware of my world.
This experience of this world creates passion and desires in me. Passion creates desire, desire creates actions, actions create reactions. And my world continues with cause and effect.
Somebody comes and says you should be investing money right now because the market is down. Then suddenly my desire to make money kicks in -- Rajan, you need to do something! And I start doing things. That creates another chain reaction when the market drops.
So Rajas is the activity which is the nature of cause and effect. My interaction with this Prakriti, because of my passion, creates activity. This activity creates the experience of joys and sorrows.
I pat my back and say Im so smart -- when everybody was thinking this way, I was doing that. Then when things go bad, I say, well, people really cheated me, they should have told me. And then Tamas -- inertia.
If we dont have inertia, we dont even exist. For something to exist in time and space, it has to have inertia. It has to remain in that condition in time and space for others to experience it.
I am real because I have inertia -- I remain in that state in time and space for others to experience me. So the inertia is the essential part of Prakriti. Tamas is the very essential quality of Prakriti. Just as Sattva and rajas.
If you take one of the three out, Prakriti does not exist. Sattva cannot exist if there is no rajas and Tamas. There is nothing to be aware of.
Rajas cannot exist if there is no inertia. But because there is inertia, Tamas, all three continue to work with each other. So this Tamas is the nature of inertia, which at my level I relate to as my sleep, deep sleep.
When I really dont want to do anything, somebody says, oh, lets go and have a party. Forget about it, Im not in the mood today -- Im overwhelmed by Tamas. If Im very sleepy and you tell me to do something, forget about it.
Right now all I want to do is sleep. That means I am overwhelmed by Tamas, and all I want to do is go back to my basic nature. Iti Gunaha Prakruti Sambhavaha -- they are part of Prakriti.
They are the nature of Prakriti, embedded into it. They are not like qualities of a material where you can say, if I test in the lab I will find Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. They are actually the moods of my mind when I interact with this Prakriti.
So sometimes my mind is overwhelmed by Sattva. Things start getting clearer to me. I tried very hard yesterday, couldnt figure it out.
This morning it suddenly came to me -- an aha moment, a Eureka moment. That is predominant Sattva. Then Rajas -- now Ive figured out, I need to do something.
And Tamas -- this is enough. I need to go to sleep. There is always a time -- no matter how dynamic a person is, he has to take rest.
Ithiguna Prakritisam Nibadnanti Mahabhaho Dehe Dehi nam Avyayaam -- this imperishable self, the Purusha, the Brahman which is imperishable, is now bound by this perishable body through these three gunas. The Purusha comes in contact with the Prakriti and gets attached to it. So this dehi in me, my consciousness which is of all-pervading, imperishable nature -- once it attaches to this body, mind and intellect and enjoys the gunas, it gets bound.
So now I consider this is me, the body; this is me, the intellect. This is only possible because the consciousness tells me thats who I am. This imperishable one is now bound in this body by these three gunas.
Tatra satvam nirmalatva Prakasakam anamayam Sukha sangena badnati gnana sangena cha anagaha -- my mind, under the influence of these three gunas, binds me to this body, this mind, and this intellect. So what is the nature of it? Now I want to unbound myself so that I can realize my imperishable self. Thats the quest we have.
So that I will have infinite happiness, unlimited happiness which Im seeking. So I have to unbound myself. So I have to see what is binding me and how.
So the first is Sattva. Tatra Sattva nirmalatva Prakashakam annamayam. The nature of Sattva is prakashakam -- suddenly things become clearer to me.
Before I walk into this room at night, its dark. Nothing is clear about whats in the room. Suddenly I switch the light on.
Everything becomes completely clear because it is luminous. Thats the nature of Sattva in my chitta, in my mind. When Sattva prevails, things start getting clearer to me.
So its the nature of luminosity. And annamayam -- eat some sattvic food. You tell Panditji this: the pure ghee, you know, cholesterol and all -- thats good for you, thats Sattva.
So purity is of the nature of health. When I am completely in tune with myself, I feel healthy and I feel aware. Everything seems nice, which is the experience of happiness and joy.
Thats what binds me to this Prakriti. When I feel I am in command and I understand things, I am enjoying this knowledge. When I learn something, it binds me to knowledge and the happiness of getting knowledge.
Sukha sangena badnati -- it binds me to happiness. Gnana sangena cha anagaha. Sattva binds me to knowledge and happiness. Its still a bondage. No matter how golden the chain is, its still a bondage.
Therefore, many other saints have argued about this. The Vedantin says this, and we say harina janato Muktina magya. Whoever among the Gujarati fellows can understand -- he says Gods people do not want this liberation.
They want birth after birth. So that I enjoy your bhakti. Because if Im not there, how can I enjoy your bhakti? Therefore Harina Jina Muktina Mangi Mangi Jana Vi Janavata.
I want birth after birth so that I can devote myself to you. Bondage to this Sattva? This experience of my devotion to my Lord is giving me happiness and ecstasy. I dont want to give it up. Just keep me in this state.
Dont take me to the next one. Otherwise I will lose this ecstasy. This is bondage to Sattva, even for a man of dynamic personality who worked 18 hours a day.

These verses expose the mechanics of Rajas and Tamas with surgical precision. Rajas is ragātmakam, born of passionate attachment, and binds through trishna (thirst) and karma-sangena (attachment to action). How often do you feel compelled to act, to achieve, to acquire? That restless drive is Rajas at work. Tamas, born of ignorance, binds through pramada (heedlessness), alasya (laziness), and nidra (sleep). Verse 9 summarizes beautifully: Sattva attaches you to happiness, Rajas to action, and Tamas, by covering knowledge, attaches you to heedlessness. Today, trace your actions back to their source: Are you acting from clarity, compulsion, or avoidance?
The teaching uses the example of forgotten money, $300 sealed in an envelope that did not exist until awareness revealed it. This illustrates Sattvas essential nature: things come into existence for you only when you become aware of them. Similarly, the whole world exists for you only through your awareness. But notice also the Rajasic trap described: setting a goal of $100,000, achieving it, yet still remaining unsatisfied, always chasing the next thing. Today, examine one goal you are pursuing: Is it Sattva seeking knowledge, Rajas seeking endless activity, or Tamas seeking escape? Can you find the witness who observes all three without being pulled by any? Remember, even the bliss of devotion (as the teaching notes about those who seek birth after birth to enjoy bhakti) is a form of bondage.
